pages.title: The proposal’s purpose
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Group organiser · simulated source
pages.subject: More regular contact
paragraphs: The organiser proposes four evening sessions per month, announced at least forty-eight hours before each session. The aim is more regular contact and fewer unresolved questions between meetings. The proposal does not yet explain whether all four sessions are essential or how someone unable to attend could contribute.

For the organiser, a workable alternative should preserve useful contact rather than simply reduce the calendar burden. Written updates and fewer live meetings may be options, but their role would need to be clear. A trial could help establish whether the combination works. These are fictional negotiating positions; neither attendance nor agreement has been recorded as a real commitment.

pages.title: The impact and the limit
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Participant’s position · simulated source
pages.subject: Participation requires planning
paragraphs: The participant supports regular contact but can commit to only two evenings per month. They need at least seven days’ notice to arrange their other responsibilities. A forty-eight-hour announcement makes attendance unreliable even when the session itself would be useful. The participant is willing to discuss updates between live sessions.

The distinction between preference and constraint matters. Accepting a lower frequency would not, by itself, make the notice period workable. A counterproposal should acknowledge the organiser’s purpose, identify what can be offered and retain the planning condition explicitly. A polite expression of interest should not be summarised as full acceptance of every term.

pages.title: Find the real sticking point
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: How do you feel about moving our group sessions to four evenings a month?
lines.audioText: How do you feel about moving our group sessions to four evenings a month?
lines.translation: O que acha de passar nossos encontros do grupo para quatro noites por mês?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I can see the value of more regular contact. Even so, four evenings would be difficult for me
lines.audioText: I can see the value of more regular contact. Even so, four evenings would be difficult for me.
lines.translation: Vejo o valor de um contato mais regular. Mesmo assim, quatro noites seriam difíceis para mim

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Is the number of sessions the main problem, or the notice?
lines.audioText: Is the number of sessions the main problem, or the notice?
lines.translation: O principal problema é a quantidade de encontros ou a antecedência?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Both. I can commit to two, and I need seven days’ notice to arrange things
lines.audioText: Both. I can commit to two, and I need seven days’ notice to arrange things.
lines.translation: Ambos. Posso me comprometer com dois e preciso de sete dias de antecedência para me organizar

questions.prompt: What are the two separate difficulties?
questions.answer: The number of sessions and short notice

pages.title: Make a counterproposal
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The proposal only gives forty-eight hours. Could you accept that occasionally?
lines.audioText: The proposal only gives forty-eight hours. Could you accept that occasionally?
lines.translation: A proposta só dá quarenta e oito horas. Aceitaria isso ocasionalmente?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Much as I’d like to be flexible, I can’t promise attendance at that notice
lines.audioText: Much as I’d like to be flexible, I can’t promise attendance at that notice.
lines.translation: Por mais que queira ser flexível, não posso prometer presença com essa antecedência

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What alternative would still give the group useful contact?
lines.audioText: What alternative would still give the group useful contact?
lines.translation: Que alternativa ainda daria um contato útil ao grupo?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Two planned live sessions, with short updates between them
lines.audioText: Two planned live sessions, with short updates between them.
lines.translation: Dois encontros ao vivo planejados, com atualizações breves entre eles

questions.answer: Two planned live sessions with short updates

pages.title: Confirm the extent of the concession
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Would you agree to a four-week trial before reviewing it?
lines.audioText: Would you agree to a four-week trial before reviewing it?
lines.translation: Concordaria com um teste de quatro semanas antes de avaliar?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, provided the dates are agreed a week ahead. The trial shouldn’t erase that limit
lines.audioText: Yes, provided the dates are agreed a week ahead. The trial shouldn’t erase that limit.
lines.translation: Sim, desde que as datas sejam combinadas uma semana antes. O teste não deveria apagar esse limite

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then the shared interest is regular contact; frequency and notice are the variables
lines.audioText: Then the shared interest is regular contact; frequency and notice are the variables.
lines.translation: Então o interesse comum é contato regular; frequência e antecedência são as variáveis

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. We can make a concession without implying that every condition is negotiable
lines.audioText: Exactly. We can make a concession without implying that every condition is negotiable.
lines.translation: Exatamente. Podemos ceder em um ponto sem sugerir que toda condição é negociável

pages.title: Negotiate a workable change
pages.instruction: Respond to the proposal and negotiate conditions that could work

pages.title: Frequency changes, notice does not
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I’ve thought about the group-session proposal. I can accept two live sessions a month instead of four, and I’m happy to try short written updates between them. I still need the dates confirmed at least seven days ahead; reducing the frequency doesn’t remove that planning need. Could we treat the two-session arrangement as a four-week trial and review whether the updates cover the gaps? We seem to agree on regular contact and a trial. The sticking point is not willingness to participate, but the notice required to make participation feasible. Please could you confirm that part explicitly before we tell the group the whole proposal has been accepted?
